stem: The student wants to present the aim of Ramanathan's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Downbursts are powerful downward gusts of air from thunderstorms that can flatten crops and endanger aircraft.
• Many downbursts are too small or too brief for conventional radar networks to detect.
• In 2023, atmospheric scientist Priya Ramanathan led a team that investigated whether low-cost wind sensors mounted on farm irrigation towers could detect downbursts.
• The team installed 140 sensors across 60 square kilometers of Nebraska farmland.
• Over one summer, the sensors recorded 23 downbursts that radar had missed.
choices: Many downbursts, gusts that can flatten crops and endanger aircraft, are too small or too brief for conventional radar to detect.
Ramanathan's team set out to determine whether inexpensive wind sensors on irrigation towers could detect downbursts.
Ramanathan's team set out to show that sensors on irrigation towers could replace radar networks for tracking thunderstorms.
Ramanathan's team found that wind sensors on irrigation towers recorded 23 downbursts that radar had missed.
explanation: The goal asks for the aim, meaning the question the study set out to answer. The notes state that aim directly: the team investigated whether low-cost sensors on irrigation towers could detect downbursts. Choice B restates that question with the words 'set out to determine whether,' which is the language of an aim, and it adds nothing the notes don't support.

A.why: You picked the background. This sentence explains why the study mattered, but it never mentions Ramanathan's study or what the study wanted to find out.

C.why: It's phrased like an aim, but it misstates the aim. The team asked whether sensors could detect downbursts. The notes never say the team wanted to replace radar or track thunderstorms in general.

D.why: This is the study's result, not its aim. You matched the goal to the wrong stage of the research: 'found' reports what happened, not what the team set out to learn.

stem: The student wants to present the conclusion of Wierzbicki's research. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Plant leaves have stomata, tiny pores through which the plant takes in carbon dioxide.
• Plants tend to grow fewer stomata when atmospheric carbon dioxide levels are high.
• Paleobotanist Tomasz Wierzbicki counted stomata on fossil ginkgo leaves from 56-million-year-old rock layers in Greenland.
• The fossil leaves had about 40 percent fewer stomata per square millimeter than modern ginkgo leaves.
• Wierzbicki concluded that carbon dioxide levels 56 million years ago were substantially higher than they are today.
choices: Fossil ginkgo leaves from Greenland had about 40 percent fewer stomata per square millimeter than modern ginkgo leaves have.
Wierzbicki counted the stomata on fossil ginkgo leaves preserved in 56-million-year-old rock layers in Greenland.
Wierzbicki concluded that ginkgo trees grew fewer stomata 56 million years ago because Greenland's climate was warmer.
Wierzbicki concluded that atmospheric carbon dioxide was substantially higher 56 million years ago than it is today.
explanation: A conclusion is what the researcher decided the evidence means. The stomata count is the evidence. Wierzbicki's conclusion is about carbon dioxide levels in the past, and Choice D states exactly that, just as the last note records it.

A.why: This is the finding, the raw result of the count, not the conclusion drawn from it. The subtlety at this level is that 'finding' and 'conclusion' are separate stages. The goal asks for what the result means, which is higher carbon dioxide.

B.why: This describes the method: what Wierzbicki did. It doesn't say what he found or what he concluded.

C.why: It uses the word 'concluded' but attributes a conclusion the notes never state. According to the notes, fewer stomata point to high carbon dioxide, not a warmer climate. This choice replaces the real cause with a different one.

stem: The student wants to present Okafor's study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Heat waves raise the risk of hospitalization for older adults who live alone.
• In 2022, the city of Marlow Falls began a program in which volunteers phone residents over 70 on days above 35°C.
• Epidemiologist Ines Okafor compared heat-related hospitalizations among 3,000 program participants and 3,000 similar nonparticipants over two summers.
• Participants were hospitalized for heat-related illness 31 percent less often than nonparticipants.
choices: Comparing 3,000 phone-call program participants with 3,000 similar nonparticipants, Okafor found that participants had 31 percent fewer heat-related hospitalizations.
Over two summers, Okafor compared heat-related hospitalizations among 3,000 participants in a phone-call program and 3,000 similar nonparticipants.
Residents in Marlow Falls' phone-call program were hospitalized for heat-related illness 31 percent less often than residents who did not take part.
Okafor's study showed that phoning older residents on hot days prevents 31 percent of all heat-related hospitalizations in Marlow Falls.
explanation: The goal has two parts: the study and its findings. Choice A covers both. It names the study (Okafor's comparison of 3,000 participants with 3,000 nonparticipants) and its result (31 percent fewer heat-related hospitalizations), and it connects them with 'found that.'

B.why: This is only half the goal. It describes the study's design but never says what the study found.

C.why: This is the other half. It gives the result but doesn't mention Okafor or her comparison, so the reader never learns about the study that produced it.

D.why: The study compared two groups of 3,000 people. It didn't measure 'all heat-related hospitalizations in Marlow Falls,' so this choice stretches a result about one sample to the whole city.

stem: The student wants to present the aim of Marchetti and Asante's research. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Indigo was the most widely used blue dye in eighteenth-century European textiles.
• Historians had long assumed that the indigo in eighteenth-century French fabrics came mainly from Caribbean plantations.
• Conservation scientists Hélène Marchetti and Kofi Asante wanted to know whether some of that indigo came instead from woad, a plant grown in France.
• They analyzed chemical impurities in dye samples from 85 surviving French garments.
• Impurities typical of woad appeared in 38 of the samples.
choices: Historians had long assumed that the indigo in eighteenth-century French fabrics came mainly from plantations in the Caribbean.
Marchetti and Asante detected impurities typical of woad in 38 of 85 dye samples from eighteenth-century French garments.
Marchetti and Asante sought to learn whether some indigo in eighteenth-century French fabrics came from woad, a French-grown plant.
Marchetti and Asante sought to confirm that the indigo in eighteenth-century French fabrics came from Caribbean plantations.
explanation: An aim is the question the researchers wanted to answer. The third note says Marchetti and Asante wanted to know whether some of the indigo came from woad. Choice C restates that question using 'sought to learn whether.'

A.why: This is the background assumption the researchers questioned. It gives the reason the study was needed, not what the researchers set out to learn.

B.why: This is the result. 'Detected' reports what the analysis found, which is a later stage of the research than the aim.

D.why: It sounds like an aim, but it reverses the real one. The researchers were testing the Caribbean assumption by asking about woad, not trying to confirm it. When two choices both start with 'sought to,' check which one matches the note.

stem: The student wants to present the conclusion that Reyes-Moreau's team reached. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Hot Jupiters are giant planets that orbit extremely close to their stars.
• One hypothesis holds that they formed farther out and migrated inward violently, scattering any smaller planets in their path.
• Astronomer Daniel Reyes-Moreau's team searched 60 hot-Jupiter systems for additional planets.
• The team detected small companion planets near the hot Jupiter in 11 of those systems.
• The team concluded that at least some hot Jupiters formed in place or migrated inward gently.
choices: One hypothesis holds that hot Jupiters formed farther from their stars and scattered smaller planets as they migrated inward.
Reyes-Moreau's team concluded that at least some hot Jupiters formed where they are now or migrated inward gently.
Reyes-Moreau's team detected small companion planets near the hot Jupiter in 11 of the 60 systems it searched.
Reyes-Moreau's team concluded that no hot Jupiter could have formed farther out and migrated inward violently.
explanation: The goal asks for the conclusion, which the last note gives: at least some hot Jupiters formed in place or migrated gently. Choice B states it and keeps the qualifier 'at least some,' and that qualifier is what separates it from the overreaching choice.

A.why: This is the background hypothesis the study tested. It describes a debate, not what the team concluded.

C.why: This is the finding, the observation the conclusion rests on. The goal asks what the team decided the observation means.

D.why: It drops the qualifier. Finding companions in 11 of 60 systems supports a claim about 'at least some' hot Jupiters, not a claim that rules out violent migration for every one of them.

stem: The student wants to present the recommendation that resulted from Lindqvist's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many distance runners stretch statically, holding each stretch for 30 seconds or more, before races.
• Sports scientist Maren Lindqvist tested how pre-run static stretching affects performance.
• Forty-eight trained runners completed 3-kilometer time trials after either static stretching or a dynamic warm-up of leg swings and skips.
• Times after static stretching averaged 2.1 percent slower.
• Lindqvist advises runners to replace pre-race static stretching with a dynamic warm-up.
choices: Lindqvist advises runners to swap the static stretching they do before races for a dynamic warm-up of leg swings and skips.
In Lindqvist's study, 3-kilometer times averaged 2.1 percent slower after static stretching than after a dynamic warm-up.
Lindqvist had 48 trained runners complete 3-kilometer time trials after either static stretching or a dynamic warm-up.
Lindqvist advises runners to avoid all stretching before races, since stretching made runners 2.1 percent slower.
explanation: A recommendation is advice, so look for the choice that tells runners what to do. Choice A gives Lindqvist's advice as the notes state it: replace static stretching with a dynamic warm-up before races.

B.why: This is the result that led to the advice, not the advice. It tells you what happened in the trials, not what runners should do.

C.why: This is the method. It describes how the study worked and contains no recommendation.

D.why: It's phrased as advice, but it goes further than Lindqvist does. Her recommendation keeps a dynamic warm-up, and only static stretching was linked to slower times. 'Avoid all stretching' isn't supported.

stem: The student wants to describe the method Haddad used in her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tel Varesh is the site of an ancient hilltop settlement.
• Archaeologists have debated whether the settlement was occupied year-round or only seasonally.
• Archaeologist Nadia Haddad examined 900 goat teeth recovered from the site's refuse pits.
• She measured growth layers in the teeth's enamel, which record the season in which an animal died.
• The teeth showed deaths in every season, suggesting that people lived at Tel Varesh year-round.
choices: Archaeologists have debated whether the hilltop settlement at Tel Varesh was occupied year-round or only seasonally.
Haddad's analysis of goat teeth suggested that the hilltop settlement at Tel Varesh was occupied year-round.
Haddad counted the goat teeth in Tel Varesh's refuse pits to estimate how many people had lived at the settlement.
Haddad measured enamel growth layers, which record season of death, in 900 goat teeth from the site's refuse pits.
explanation: A method is what the researcher actually did. According to the notes, Haddad measured enamel growth layers in 900 goat teeth, and those layers show when each animal died. Choice D describes that procedure and explains why it is useful.

A.why: This is the background debate. It explains why the question mattered but says nothing about how Haddad studied it.

B.why: This is the study's conclusion. It names the goat teeth in passing but reports what the analysis suggested, not how the analysis was done.

C.why: It describes a method, but not Haddad's. She measured growth layers to find out the season of death. According to the notes, she didn't count teeth to estimate population.

stem: The student wants to present Varma's study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Artificial light at night can disrupt the behavior of nocturnal insects.
• Ecologist Sunita Varma wanted to know whether streetlights affect how often moths visit night-blooming flowers.
• Her team compared 20 meadow plots lit by LED streetlights with 20 unlit plots.
• Flowers in the lit plots received 58 percent fewer moth visits than flowers in the unlit plots.
choices: Varma's team compared moth visits to night-blooming flowers in 20 meadow plots lit by LED streetlights and in 20 unlit plots.
Varma set out to learn whether streetlights affect how often moths visit the flowers of night-blooming plants in meadows.
Comparing lit and unlit meadow plots, Varma's team found that flowers under LED streetlights got 58 percent fewer moth visits.
Varma's study found that LED streetlights reduce the pollination of all night-blooming plants by about 58 percent.
explanation: The goal asks for the study and its findings, so the answer has to name the study and its result together. Choice C does both. It identifies the comparison between lit and unlit plots, then reports the finding of 58 percent fewer moth visits, joined by 'found that.'

A.why: This covers only the study. It describes the comparison thoroughly but never gives the result.

B.why: This is the aim. It tells you what Varma wanted to learn, but not how she studied it or what she found.

D.why: The study measured moth visits in 40 meadow plots. It didn't measure pollination, and it didn't cover all night-blooming plants. This choice claims more than the data show.
